examples.text: These hot dogs are pretty good, eh?
Well, what dost thou think then of seeing the world? Do ye wish to go round Cape Horn to see any more of it, eh? Can’t ye see the world where you stand?

raw_glosses: (informal, chiefly Canada, Upper Midwestern US, New Zealand, Australia, UK, Ireland, South Africa, India, Hong Kong, Singapore, Commonwealth) Used as a tag question, to emphasise what goes before or to request that the listener express an opinion about what has been said.
glosses: Used as a tag question, to emphasise what goes before or to request that the listener express an opinion about what has been said.

examples.text: —I've been studying Graphiurus murinus. —Eh? Studying what?

glosses: In isolation, a request for repetition or clarification of what has just been said.

examples.text: —You're going to be a dad! —Eh? You're joking!

glosses: In isolation, expressing surprise or confusion

examples.text: I went to the restaurant, eh, but my friends didn't show up.

raw_glosses: (chiefly Canada) An interjection used to ascertain the continued attention of someone addressed by the speaker.
glosses: An interjection used to ascertain the continued attention of someone addressed by the speaker.

examples.text:
—Do you feel like going out tonight?
—Eh, I don't know.
“Look, Mom; I made the real rocket, based on the macaroni prototype!” “…Eh.”

glosses: Expressing apathy or lack of enthusiasm; meh.

examples.text:

—Eh, It's like that eh.
